assessmentSummary.identity: A supported supine breathing exercise with hips and knees near 90 degrees and a bilateral ceiling reach throughout one comfortable inhale, longer unforced exhale, and reset. Feet-on-wall and fully-supported lower-leg interfaces are exact variants; hands-on-ribs no-reach breathing and active hip-lift/ball/balloon breathing are distinct definitions.
currentCardFindings: The existing card describes the supine support and reach clearly but overstates a universal rib-down or pelvic-position outcome and does not define support stability, breath duration, permitted effort, dizziness rules, or dosage boundaries.

The archived Hip Reset source omits support, heel pressure, hip lift, pelvic shift, reach, ball or balloon, breath cycle, completion, and reset facts; it remains an identity quarantine and must not be guessed into the reach or balloon card.

The prior generic 20/10 score obscured the difference between exercise complexity and physical difficulty. The exact wall-supported reach proposal is 26/8/26, while fully supported lower legs reduce it to 22/5/22.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: breathing stays calm and repeatable without strain, dizziness, shoulder shrug, back discomfort, or support movement

coachCues: Let the support carry your legs
athleteInstructions: Lie on your back with your legs fully supported near 90/90
Reach your hands toward the ceiling
Breathe in gently through your nose
Exhale slowly while reaching a little longer
Pause only if comfortable, then let the next inhale arrive

calibrationEvidence.uncertainty: No trial establishes a unique difficulty score, sport-transfer effect, or universal pelvic-position outcome for this exact supported reach variant.

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain one supported supine 90/90 bilateral-reach definition with exact feet-on-wall and fully-supported lower-leg variants. Keep the under-specified Hip Reset source quarantined. Author hands-on-ribs no-reach lateral expansion and active heel-pull/hip-lift/ball/balloon breathing as distinct definitions. Treat only cycle count, comfortable cadence, rest, and reach effort within the exact action as delivery annotations; avoid structural-reset, treatment, recovery, or transfer claims.

currentCardSnapshot.description: A supported supine breath-cycle exercise with hips and knees near 90 degrees and both arms reaching toward the ceiling. One exact variant plants both feet on a stable wall; another fully supports the lower legs on a stable bench or box. A repetition is one comfortable inhale and longer unforced exhale while the bilateral reach, neck, support contact, rib cage, pelvis, and lumbar region remain within the declared quality contract.

environment.changeRule: Wall versus lower-leg support requires an exact variant. Removing or unilateralizing the reach, adding a hip lift, ball, balloon, limb motion, resistance, or breath hold changes identity or requires separate review.

claims: Functional Movement Systems directly specifies a supine feet-on-wall 90/90 breathing cycle with hands on the lower lateral abdomen or ribs; it does not include an arm reach.

Supported 90/90 Breathing with Bilateral Reach retains the audited legacy bilateral reach as an identity-bearing action. Hands-on-ribs no-reach breathing and active hip-lift/ball/balloon breathing therefore remain distinct cards, and the ambiguous Hip Reset source stays quarantined.
The direct instruction establishes supine support, hips and knees near 90 degrees, a breath cycle, and fixed contact positions rather than spinal rotation.

Classify Supported 90/90 Breathing with Bilateral Reach as supported breath control, bilateral reach, and static trunk organization; declare wall-foot versus fully-supported lower-leg contact as exact variants.

evidence.sourceTitle: Stabilizing function of the diaphragm: dynamic MRI and synchronized spirometric assessment
claims: Dynamic MRI in 30 healthy adults supports ventilatory and postural diaphragm behavior during limb tasks, but it is not a trial of this exercise and does not quantify individual muscle force.

Represent diaphragm, intercostals, abdominal wall, rib cage, spine, pelvis, supported hips and knees, scapular protraction, shoulder-position demand, and cervical stabilization without promising structural change.

evidence.sourceTitle: Stabilizing function of the diaphragm: dynamic MRI and synchronized spirometric assessment
claims: Breathing and limb-position demands can coexist, but the cited laboratory task does not establish one optimal rib, lumbar, or pelvic posture for all participants.
Keep the bilateral reach, declared support, and comfortable breath cycle exact; invalidate shrugging, crunching, forced flattening, support loss, hip lift, heel pull, or added equipment.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: Published diaphragmatic-breathing protocols and outcomes are highly heterogeneous, and no source assigns a Vortex difficulty score or participant classification.
The review-only wall-supported proposal is 26 exercise complexity and 8 physical difficulty; fully supported lower legs reduce support management to 22 and 5. Overall is derived as the maximum.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: Low external load does not mean zero exposure, and the systematic review reports variable protocols with safety information often underreported.

Track support pressure, reach time, breath effort, invalid or symptom-limited cycles, prior trunk and shoulder work, total supine time, and recovery as a conservative planning estimate rather than a biological guarantee.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
evidence.sourcePublisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
claims: ACOG advises avoiding prolonged supine exercise after 20 weeks of pregnancy and individualizing activity; that general guidance is not clearance for this card.

Require a stable wall or braced bench/box, safe floor access, comfortable supine position and reach, unforced resting breathing, symptom reporting, and a separately reviewed non-supine option when indicated.
VA guidance uses a comfortable nasal inhale and a longer controlled exhale and allows position progression; it does not establish one universal workout dose for this reach card.
Use a small dose of comfortable cycles with rest as needed, count invalid and symptom-limited attempts as exposure, and recompute duration from actual cadence, pauses, rest, setup, and substitutions.

The direct source specifies stable wall support, hips and knees near 90 degrees, comfortable neck and spine, nasal inhale, longer exhale, pause, and relaxation, while the audited legacy source adds bilateral reach.
Instructions must declare the exact support variant, bilateral reach, comfortable inhale, longer unforced exhale, no crunch or hip lift, valid reset, symptom stop, and safe floor exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: The health effects of diaphragmatic breathing: A systematic review
claims: The review found substantial protocol heterogeneity and incomplete safety reporting, so absence of reported harm does not establish universal safety.

Do not force breath depth, exhale, or retention. Stop for pain, dizziness, faintness, chest pain, unusual shortness of breath, panic, air hunger, neurologic symptoms, cramp, support movement, or inability to reset comfortably.

evidence.sourceTitle: How Breath-Control Can Change Your Life: A Systematic Review on Psycho-Physiological Correlates of Slow Breathing
claims: Slow breathing can influence cardiorespiratory and autonomic measures, but protocols and mechanisms vary.

Use the card as low-intensity breathing practice or a transition to comfortable post-session breathing; do not promise nervous-system reset, structural repositioning, recovery acceleration, or sport-performance transfer.
VA instructions use simple position, inhale, and exhale language and advance only as control becomes comfortable.
Athlete support must identify the exact leg support, bilateral reach, expected low effort, comfortable breath, self-checks, unexpected symptoms, stop signal, and safe exit without clinical promises.
The direct setup provides observable support, hand or arm position, cadence, and relaxation checkpoints.

Coach support must distinguish the two support variants and observe reach, neck and shoulder tension, breath strain, support pressure, rib and pelvic comfort, symptoms, valid reset, duration, and floor exit.

evidence.sourceTitle: Physical Activity and Exercise During Pregnancy and the Postpartum Period
evidence.sourcePublisher: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists
claims: Supine positioning is not universally appropriate, and pregnancy guidance requires individualization rather than a generic age or exercise-level cutoff.

Offer exact lower-leg support, comfortable joint angles, head support, fewer cycles, longer rest, multimodal instruction, or a separately reviewed non-supine substitution; removing the reach selects a different card.

evidence.sourceTitle: The Value of Blowing Up a Balloon
evidence.sourcePublisher: North American Journal of Sports Physical Therapy
claims: The published ball-and-balloon sequence explicitly adds heel pull, a small pelvic lift, knee-ball pressure, right arm overhead, left-hand balloon control, and repeated resisted exhalation.

Those actions define a separate card. Hands-on-ribs no-reach breathing is also distinct; wall versus fully-supported lower legs remain exact reach variants, while cycle count, comfortable cadence, rest, and effort are delivery annotations.
